DOC-0004 Verification Protocol — Amplitude Control

Verification Protocol — Amplitude Control

This document is the verification protocol for amplitude control. The procedures in it are Verification Protocol entities (VER-), and its devices, equipment and requirements are gathered from them by live query blocks (provenance-ddf DES-0032), so revising a procedure revises this document with it. Results are reported in DOC-0005.

Purpose

To show, by bench test, that the NeuroPulse system adjusts stimulation amplitude on the evoked response as its requirements state, and that it never exceeds the 8 mA ceiling under a single fault. The procedures here are written to be executed as they stand: an execution that passes every step is objective evidence that the requirements it verifies are met.

Scope

The requirements this protocol verifies, each through the procedure that declares it verifies it:

☑ REQ-0001 Closed-loop amplitude adjustment approved · verified by VER-0001
☑ REQ-0002 Single-fault amplitude ceiling approved · verified by VER-0002

Requirements no procedure verifies yet are out of scope for this revision, listed by ID:

  • REQ-0003

The subsystem allocation REQ-0003 is verified at the system level through REQ-0002, whose single-fault procedure exercises the ASIC's current limit; its own inspection of the ASIC design is left to a later revision of this protocol.

Device Under Test

Every device an approved procedure in this protocol is run on, each listed once with the procedures that test it, in Table 1:

A procedure names the part it tests, not a particular build: the build each execution was run on is recorded with its result and listed in the report.

Test equipment

All procedures run on the bench, with the implant in a saline tank. The equipment the approved procedures need, each listed once with the procedures that need it:

EQP-0001 Bench ECAP simulator, Neurolab ES-4 · needed by VER-0001
EQP-0002 Precision current probe, Tekbench CP-30 · needed by VER-0001
EQP-0003 Fault-injection lead simulator, Neurolab FL-2 · needed by VER-0002

Each unit used must be within its calibration interval on the day of execution. The units used, by serial number, are recorded with each execution, not here, since the same procedure may be run again on different units.

Procedures

The approved procedures, in author-assigned order:

VER-0001 Bench verification of closed-loop amplitude adjustment

approved · verifies REQ-0001

Apply a simulated ECAP response via bench stimulator, confirm the algorithm under test (DES-0001) adjusts delivered amplitude to hold the response within the configured target band across three representative response profiles.

Device under testCMP-0001: NeuroPulse implantable pulse generator
Equipment neededEQP-0001: Bench ECAP simulator
EQP-0002: Precision current probe

Steps

StepDescriptionAcceptance criteria

Place the implant in the saline tank, connect its sense electrode to the bench ECAP simulator and clip the precision current probe onto the stimulation lead. Program a fixed amplitude of 3 mA in open loop.

The simulator detects an evoked response on every stimulation cycle, and the probe reads 3 mA ± 2 %.

Configure the target band from the clinician settings and enable closed-loop control.

The implant reports closed-loop mode, and the target band it reads back matches the band configured.

Replay response profile 1, posture change from supine to standing, for 10 minutes.

The evoked response is within the target band on at least 99 % of cycles, and delivered amplitude stays within the configured range.

Replay response profile 2, a slow increase in neural sensitivity, for 10 minutes.

The evoked response is within the target band on at least 99 % of cycles, and delivered amplitude stays within the configured range.

Replay response profile 3, transient responses from coughing, for 10 minutes.

The evoked response returns to the target band within 5 cycles of each transient, and delivered amplitude stays within the configured range.

Executions

  • EVD-0001: Execution record — closed-loop amplitude adjustment bench test — 2026-08-04, against commit 145edd3, pass

VER-0002 Bench verification of single-fault amplitude ceiling

approved · verifies REQ-0002

Simulate sense-electrode lead disconnection during active stimulation and confirm delivered amplitude never exceeds 8 mA, exercising the hardware current-limit circuit (REQ-0003) independent of firmware behavior.

ECO-0001 added the lead-disconnection fault injection step; before it the procedure covered only a firmware-commanded overrange attempt.

Device under testCMP-0001: NeuroPulse implantable pulse generator
Equipment neededEQP-0003: Fault-injection lead simulator

Steps

StepDescriptionAcceptance criteria

Connect the implant's sense electrode through the fault-injection lead simulator, with its current monitor on the stimulation lead. Enable closed-loop control with the amplitude at its configured maximum.

The current monitor reads the configured maximum amplitude, within ± 2 %.

Through the test interface, command an amplitude of 10 mA, above the ceiling.

Delivered amplitude does not exceed 8 mA.

Disconnect the sense electrode during active stimulation, hold for 30 seconds and reconnect. Repeat for ten trials.

Delivered amplitude does not exceed 8 mA at any time in any of the ten trials.

Executions

  • EVD-0002: Execution record — single-fault amplitude ceiling bench test — 2026-08-11, against commit 145edd3, pass

Acceptance criteria

Each step above carries its own acceptance criteria, and a procedure passes only when every one of its steps does. A step that does not is a failure of the procedure: the execution is recorded as fail, not repeated until it passes. The single-fault condition VER-0002 injects is that of [1].

Records

Each execution is recorded as Verification Evidence (EVD-), naming the procedure it tests, the commit of this repository holding the procedure as it was run, the build of the device under test it was run on, its date, its overall result, a result and pass or fail for each step, and the equipment used with each item's serial number and calibration due date. The procedure's versions are its git history, not a number kept by hand. A procedure revised after it was executed must be executed again. A procedure is revised through a change request, as ECO-0001 revised VER-0002.
